sections.section_name: Section B - Art Elements & Conceptual Terms

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 'Pramanam' as one of the essential Six Limbs of Indian Painting (Shadang). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Pramanam refers to the structural laws of proportion, measure, and structural anatomy. It ensures that visual elements are harmoniously balanced and correctly scaled relative to one another.

questions.question_text: Describe how 'Texture' is utilized as a fundamental element of visual art. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Texture represents the surface quality of an artwork, whether actual (tactile) or implied (visual). It provides structural depth, simulating how an object might feel if physically touched.

questions.question_text: What does the aesthetic term 'Lavanya Yojanam' signify in the traditional Shadang framework? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Lavanya Yojanam translates to the infusion of grace and artistic elegance. It adds aesthetic charm and emotional structural beauty to a painting, elevating it beyond mere accurate representation.

questions.question_text: Define 'Form' as a core structural element of three-dimensional sculpture. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Form refers to an object's three-dimensional structural mass, exhibiting height, width, and depth. In sculpture, it strictly defines the physical volume and spatial boundaries occupied by the artwork.

questions.question_text: Explain the role of 'Negative Space' in a compositional painting layout. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Negative space is the empty structural area surrounding the primary subjects. It provides visual breathing room, emphasizes the main figures, and creates essential balance within the compositional frame.

questions.question_text: Appreciate the aesthetic and iconographic features of the Chola Bronze sculpture of 'Nataraja' depicting the cosmic dance of Lord Shiva. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Nataraja bronze gracefully portrays Shiva balancing on the dwarf of ignorance (Apasmara) within a flaming aureole (prabhamandala). His four hands hold a drum and fire, while forming gestures of protection and liberation, displaying dynamic balance, metallurgical mastery, and deep spiritual symbolism.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the structural and architectural layout of the 'Kailashnath Temple' at Ellora, focusing on its unique rock-cut excavation technique. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Kailashnath Temple is an architectural marvel carved from a single basalt cliff using a top-down monolithic excavation technique. Designed in the Dravidian style, its sprawling courtyard, multi-story vimana, towering pillars, and intricate relief sculptures demonstrate unparalleled spatial planning and sculptural grandeur.

questions.question_text: Describe the structural evolution and key architectural features of the 'Taj Mahal' as a prime example of Indo-Islamic tomb architecture. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Built entirely of white marble, the Taj Mahal represents the pinnacle of Mughal architecture. It rests on a raised plinth featuring perfect bilateral symmetry, a massive double dome, four corner minarets, and exquisite pietra dura inlay, beautifully blending Persian layout proportions with Indian craftsmanship.
